comments.text: Startup literal normally calls clear_statics, which leaves the next callee in r3. The payload loader changes it to a one-time stub in the cleared zero tail.
Directory classifier takes a FAT entry pointer at +0 and the UTF-16 name at +0x12. WAV is type 11, unsupported is -1. The FLAC hook moves the entry and resumes stock at 0x0C03EBA0.
The two USB open size calls at 0x0C055324 and 0x0C05542C share this pool word. The callee takes a file handle and a length output pointer.
USB audio close reads this pool at 0x0C055472. The mod releases the virtual FLAC file slot and closes the stock file.
WAV PCM read pool, reader 0x0C05591A. FLAC supplies little-endian virtual WAV samples for its active USB handle.

INFO side of the display mode switch. Sets staging 0x0C9B818C bit 7 and clears 0x0C9B818F bit 2. The BROWSE path at 0x0C05FC8A clears INFO and sets BROWSE. These become page 5 frame 2 byte 6 bit 7 and page 4 frame 2 byte 6 bit 2 respectively.
Writes the PLAY/PAUSE lamp to bit 4 of staging 0x0C9B8190 (page 4 frame 2 byte 9). Paused and playing captures confirm the flashed and steady phases.
Sets CUE (bit 3 of page 4 frame 2 byte 9). The CUE indicator is steady after setting a cue while PLAY/PAUSE flashes.
Sets the shared BEAT LOOP LED (D515) in bit 3 of staging 0x0C9B8191, serialized to page 4 frame 2 byte 10. The beat-loop capture isolated it from the RELOOP/EXIT lamp in bit 0.

Updates LOOP IN and LOOP OUT (bits 5 and 6 of staging 0x0C9B8190, page 4 frame 2 byte 9). The loop-out-adjust capture holds bit 5 clear and flashes bit 6, matching the operating instructions. The update initializes both bits high at 0x0C060180 before applying the timed states.
Sets the RELOOP/EXIT lamp in bit 0 of staging 0x0C9B8191 (page 4 frame 2 byte 10). The bit comes on when setting a loop out point and stays set after LOOP EXIT while the loop is available.

Panel source LED packing. DISC source is page 4 frame 2 byte 10 bit 1. USB sets byte 9 bit 7 and clears the DISC lamp at 0x0C0605B8..5BC. COMPUTER/PC sets byte 9 bit 2 at 0x0C0605CE. Verified by switching the sources and entering CONTROL MODE.
Sets the DISC EJECT lamp (page 4 frame 2 byte 10 bit 6) during the eject operation. The drive/eject capture alternates this bit while EJECT is displayed.

USB STOP lamp helper writes staging 0x0C9B8190 bit 1 (page 4 frame 2 byte 9). An attached, recognized stick lights the bit, USB STOP clears it, and the no-media control run leaves it off. The USB source lamp at bit 7 remains independent.

Writes the BPM LOCK legend flag in staging 0x0C9B818F bit 3 (page 4 frame 2 byte 6 bit 3). The BPM display helper can clear the same bit later for a dark flash phase. Confirmed by storing a master BPM on a 128 BPM WAV and toggling BPM LOCK.

CDJ-350 tempo range selectors in staging 0x0C9B818E / page 6 frame 2 byte 7: load limit 200 -> bit 6 (+/-10), 300 -> bit 7 (+/-6), 320 -> bit 5 (+/-16). At full positive fader travel the readout gives +10, +6 and +16 respectively. WIDE uses bit 2 with bit 4 clear.
CDJ-350 display sign packing. Positive tempo sets bits 1 and 0 of 0x0C9B818F, negative sets bit 1 only. That byte appears as frame 2 byte 6 on page 4.

CDJ-350 MAIN TX indicator checksum. Each of the six 32-byte slots at 0x0C9B850C stores the low 8 bits of the sum of slot bytes 0..27 at slot byte 28 (frame 2 byte 12). Slot bytes 29..31 are zero. The text slot bypasses this loop. Confirmed against SCIF1 captures.

Starts packing six CDJ-350 indicator pages with paired headers 0x11/0x12 through 0x61/0x62. Frame 2 byte 11 of pages 1 and 2 carries track tens and units, from 0x0C9B8170 and 0x0C9B8171. The separate 0x0C9B85CC slot holds two text rows of 16 wire bytes.
Page 3 frame 2 bytes 6..11 copy the six raw seven-segment masks for MM SS FF (75 frames/sec), from 0x0C9B8170 offsets 7, 6, 15, 14, 13, 12. Segment A..G masks are 01, 02, 10, 40, 20, 04, 08.

Packs page 4 frame 2 bytes 6..10 from the CDJ-350 display staging buffer. Byte 6 bit 2 is BROWSE and bit 3 is LOCK (BPM LOCK ON/OFF capture; preserves the firmware flash phase). Byte 9 LED masks: 02 USB STOP, 04 COMPUTER, 08 CUE, 10 PLAY/PAUSE, 20 LOOP IN, 40 LOOP OUT, 80 USB source. Byte 10: 01 RELOOP/EXIT, 02 DISC source, 08 BEAT LOOP, 10 MASTER TEMPO, 20 VINYL, 40 DISC EJECT. Confirmed with SCIF1 input sequences.

Page 5 frame 2 byte 6 carries A.CUE (bit 0), BPM display (bit 3), tempo decimal placement (bits 4 and 5), and INFO (bit 7). Bytes 7, 9 and 11 carry the remaining BPM digits, and bytes 8 and 10 carry the tempo fraction. Toggling DISPLAY between track list and track information confirmed the INFO flag.

Page 6 frame 2 byte 6 bit 0 is REMAIN. Byte 7 encodes the tempo range: while bit 4 is set, bits 7, 6, and 5 select +/-6, +/-10 and +/-16 respectively. WIDE uses bit 2 with bit 4 clear. Verified at the positive fader limit (9B, 5B, 3B, 0F respectively) and by engaging BPM LOCK, which set 3B. Bytes 8..11 carry the playing-address bar; the low 30 bits map left to right.
Computes the CDJ-350 playing-address position on a 30-segment scale. The selected four-byte pattern is written to display staging offsets 0x18..0x1B, then serialized as page 6 frame 2 bytes 8..11.
Copies the A.CUE setting from 0x0C9B8DDC bit 0 into display byte 0x0C9B818C bit 0 (page 5 frame 2 byte 6). Verified by holding TIME MODE/AUTO CUE and diffing SCIF1 captures.
WAV header reader pool, read at 0x0C08311C and 0x0C083184. FLAC synthesizes a 16-bit PCM WAV header at the source sample rate.
NOR word-programming path. During an emulated USB update with a changed version, the flash task advanced through 64 KiB sectors while polling and programming through the uncached flash mirror.

USB update reads the version at file offset 0x60010. In the version-checked mode it skips programming if the first character is at least ASCII 1 and it and the two digits after the dot match the running label. The checked mode starts at flash 0x60000 and writes 57 sectors. A stock v1.14 to modified v1.15 update reached COMPLETE and the emulator NOR readback matched the playback image. The NOR readback matched through 0x3EFFFF. Differences outside the update window were at flash 0x3F8000–0x3F8017 and 0x3FFFFC–0x3FFFFF.
MAIN startup clears SDRAM from 0x0C1CC678 through 0x0DCC2D33 using the bounds at 0x0C139864. The FLAC loader runs before this clear and copies to the uncached SDRAM mirror.

CDJ-350 1 ms tick group: increments u32 tick_ms (0x0CD2DCC0), then calls keys_tick_1ms (0x0C0C6EBC) and the other 1 ms routines from pools 0x0C0AE44C..0x0C0AE468. Reached through 0x0C0BB1DA, whose pointer sits at 0x0C1778D0 right after the CMT0 (vector 142) entry at 0x0C1778BC; the board's CMT0 tick is 1 ms (CMCOR 0x1045, Pphi/8). In the emulator under host load it ran about 600 times per emulated second instead of 1000 (the CDJ-850's tick_1ms the same) [emu].
mp3ActTask entry. Its descriptor at 0x0C176C88 reserves a 0x1800-byte stack. FLAC uses a private stack for the decoder.
Audio open redirect pool, read at 0x0C0B30CE. On USB the FLAC hook exposes WAV as the extension after the stock open.
Second audio open redirect pool, read at 0x0C0B360C and 0x0C0B372C.

CDJ-350 counterpart of the CDJ-850's panel_unpack_buttons (0x0C0D610C): frame 1 bytes 1..14 and frame 2 bytes 1..6 become ten big-endian words w0..w9 at 0x0CD48494 (the CDJ-850 takes frame 2 bytes 1..12, w0..w12). In player_source_mode (0x0CD48D0E) != 0, e.g. on USB, the event counter 0x0CD484F0 counts the calls: below 3 the call clears player_panel_event (0x0CD48C14) unless w1, w6 bit 0x20 or w7..w9 changed against a saved copy, so a change in any other bit (the encoder push, w6 0x0100) reaches the key build only on every third panel event [static + emu, gdb breakpoints].
CDJ-350 key tick, once per tick_1ms: counts its calls and every 100th call subtracts 100 from each u16 in key_hold_timers (0x0CD48556) that is above 0 (0x0C0C73C0..0x0C0C74A2) [static + emu].

CDJ-350 key handler shared by the player states (gate keys_handler_gate 0x0C0DC9B4, else 0x0C0C981C). Compares K0..K2 (0x0CD48508) with keys_k0_prev (0x0CD48510). Source keys act on a hold: the press edge sets a key_hold_timers entry to 1000 (DISC +0xA, USB +0xC, K2.0 +0xE) and a key_hold_pending bit (DISC byte+1 bit1, USB byte+1 bit0, K2.0 byte+5 bit0); while the key stays down and the timer reaches 0 the bit is cleared and the source change runs, after the guards 0x0CD48C01..03 != 1, 0x0CD48D1B..1D != 0xFF, 0x0CD48582 != -1, 0x0C7E4EF0 == 0, 0x0CD48BD4 == 0. USB from disc (active_source_index 0) calls 0x0C0DBDF4 then 0x0C0DBFF0. A release first clears both. So USB/DISC need about 1 s held (1000 timer units). Encoder push (panel_w6 0x0100 vs panel_w6_prev): the press sets timer +2 to 1000 and key_hold_pending byte+6 bit0 (or sets 0x0C1D5138 when 0x0CD48BE1 == 0, 0x0CD48BE2 == 2, 0x0CD4843D != 1, 0x0C1CAF1A <= 1); the action runs on release while timer +2 is still above 0 (0x0C0C94A8) [static + emu]. active_source_index (0x0CD48D06): 0 = disc, 2 = USB (after a 1 s USB hold) [emu].

CDJ-350 player step after the key build: calls 0x0C0D9006, masks K0 &= 3, K1 &= 4, K2 &= 0xB while 0x0CD48C33 == 1, then (0x0CD48D0E == 0) dispatches on player_state_by_source[active_source_index] through the table at 0x0C0DA354 (states 0..14) [static].

CDJ-350 counterpart of 0x0C0ECCB4: builds K0..K2 from w7..w9. K0: w7.9 PLAY(13), w7.10 CUE(14), w7.11 LOOP IN(12), w7.12 LOOP OUT(11), w7.13 RELOOP(10), w7.14 K0.9 and w7.15 K0.8 (the two halves of the BEAT LOOP / LOOP DIVIDE rocker: either starts a 4-beat loop [emu]), w8.9 TRACK-(2), w8.10 TRACK+(3), w8.11 SEARCH-(5), w8.12 SEARCH+(4), w9.0 USB(0), w9.1 DISC(1). K1: w8.1 VINYL(10), w8.3 TEMPO(9), w8.2 MASTER TEMPO(8), w9.9 BACK(3), w8.0 EJECT(2). K2: w9.8 TIME(13), w8.8 MENU(12), w9.10 K2.4 (PLAYLIST), w7.8 STOP(3), w7.0 K2.2 (BPM LOCK), w7.1 K2.1 (no CDJ-350 key), w9.2 K2.0 (PC; CDJ-850 LINK). Names are the CDJ-850 keys with the same K bit. w1 rotary, w2/w3 tempo fader and centre, w6 bit 0x20/0x40 as on the CDJ-850. On a loaded USB track, K2.4 produced ADD TO / NEW PLAYLIST, confirming the PLAYLIST button.
Latches 1 (USB) or 2 (DISC) into 0x0C1CAF3D after the power-on keys are read. The service gate keeps stock audio calls while this or the pending byte 0x0C1CAF4A is nonzero.

CDJ-350 player loop (inside a larger function): waits on event flag 6, copies new_keys_flag (0x0CD48C15) to 0x0CD48BE0 and clears it, and when player_panel_event (0x0CD48C14) is set builds the key words with panel_keys_to_internal_words (0x0C0DA740) only if keys_build_busy (0x0CD48BED) is 0; otherwise the event is dropped (in mode 0x0CD48D0E == 1 it is kept in 0x0CD48C21). Then calls player_dispatch_by_state. A key change that arrives while keys_build_busy blips to 1 is lost until the next panel change [static + emu]. The loop calls the unpacker itself (pool 0x0C0DAD14 -> 0x0C0C6804) and waits on event flag 6, pattern 0x37 (wai_flg from 0x0C0DAC66) [emu].

CDJ-350 player request with a blocking wait: sets keys_build_busy (0x0CD48BED) = 1, posts request 0xF through 0x0C0C7850, waits on event flag 6 bit 0 with no timeout (0x0C0BE4A4), clears it (0x0C0BE43C), then receives mailbox 7 (0x0C0BFC00). Reached on the USB source change [static].
Base pointer for the 44.1 kHz big-endian PCM ring at 0x0C1D7710. The emulator probe reads the 2352-byte sector slots here.
CDJ-350: SCIF1 at 0xFFFE8800 as clock-synchronous slave for the panel CPU (IC501), as the CDJ-850's 0x0C0F9F14. Registered from the init table at 0x0C0D6CF0.

CDJ-350 IRQ5 (vector 69, PNL_XBUSY) ISR: sets RX page 1 and sends the first 16 bytes of the indexed TX slot at 0x0C9B850C. The ISR sends prebuilt bytes; the six indicator slots get their checksums in the packer at 0x0C06904C. The seventh slot at 0x0C9B85CC is the FL text, one row of 16 wire bytes per frame.

CDJ-350 TXI1 (vector 199) ISR. Page 1: accepts RX when the 8-bit end-around-carry sum of bytes 0..14 equals byte 15 and copies it to 0x0CD48474. Page 2: sum of bytes 0..6 in byte 7, copied to 0x0CD48484. No type byte is checked. Page 2 sends the slot's second 16 bytes; after it the slot index advances 0..6 and panel_rx_changed may set flag (6,4).

CDJ-350: compares RX bytes 3..22 of the 32-byte frame pair with the previous copy (bytes 6 and 8 only bits 0x0C, checksums ignored); returns 1 on a change. Bytes 6 and 8 are the tempo slider and centre ADC low bytes; their bits 0x0C count as a change, so on the unit ADC noise keeps panel events coming, which the encoder push relies on (see 0x0C0C6804). A noise-free panel loses pushes [emu].
Writes associative operand cache address-array entries to purge buffers for USB DMA. The CDJ-350 FLAC folder/playback run reported zero coherency findings and no model warnings.

CDJ-350 floating-point polyphase synthesis (32-band windowing into 0x800-byte history buffers): by its shape the MP3 decoder's synthesis filterbank. The hottest code while an MP3 track loads or plays in the emulator, where the SH-2A FPU is emulated in software: the test stick's MP3 took about 40 s to load [emu profile].

CDJ-350 FL messages: 16-byte entries already in wire format (0x0A 0x0A + 13 characters + 0x00), the same layout as the text slot frames at 0x0C9B85CC. NO USB MEM is used from 0x0C062ED0, DISC and EMPTY from about 0x0C06124C.

CDJ-350 auto 4-beat loop handler (BEAT LOOP rocker): computes out frame from bpm_base_tenths (0x0C9B8E24) and sends audio_send_cmd(0x1e, ...). Pool words 0x0C0CE8B4 (next_sector) and 0x0C0CEBCC (audio_send_cmd) are redirected by quant_loops [static + emu].

CDJ-350 manual LOOP IN / LOOP OUT paths in keys_state3_playing: LOOP IN reads next_sector via pool words 0x0C0D1380 and 0x0C0D2728 (and 0x0C0D31B8 in state 4); LOOP OUT sends audio_send_cmd(cmd=1, mode=3, sector=play_sector) via pool words 0x0C0D1688, 0x0C0D1984, and 0x0C0D1BB8 (redirected by quant_loops) [static + emu].
CDJ-350 state-4 looping key handler (keys_state4_looping), jumped to via pool word 0x0C0C7F7C at 0x0C0C7D92 (redirected by quant_loops_drift for per-pass loop drift correction) [static + emu].

CDJ-350 USB-B (PC mode) device descriptor: USB 2.00, EP0 64 bytes, vid 0x08E4, pid 0x0156, bcdDevice 0x0114 (the CDJ-850 v1.13 has pid 0x0157, bcdDevice 0x0113). Holding PC shows CONTROL MODE and the port enumerates with MIDI IN 0x83 and HID 0x87/0x06; PLAY sends MIDI note 0, CUE note 1 [emu].

Loop state (player state 4) handler for the BEAT LOOP (LOOP DIVIDE) rocker. K0.8 (wire w7 0x8000, '+') copies loop_divide_count (0x0C1AB7D8) to loop_divide_prev_count (0x0C1AB7DC) and decrements the count if it is above 0. A K0.8 hold of more than 400 ms restores the previous count. Nothing happens while beat_lamp_loop_in (0x0C1AB7D0) is -1. In the emulator, two '-' presses moved the count from 0 to 2 [emu].

K0.9 (wire w7 0x4000, '-') in the loop state saves the count and increments loop_divide_count up to 6, one halving per press. In play (state 3, 0x0C0D1A50/0x0C0D1BEA) either rocker half starts a 4-beat loop instead. Neither path writes the loop points (loop_in_frames 0x0CD48D7C, loop_out_frames 0x0CD48CCC). The count instead acts in the audio feeder through loop_divide_position (0x0C01662E). With the 128 BPM stick, count 1 made the kick repeat every half beat while the loop and time display stayed 4 beats [emu].

Returns pos modulo (beat segment length / 2^loop_divide_count), with count 0..6 giving divisors 1..64. While one of two module flags (0x0C1AB7E0, 0x0C1AB7E4) is 1 the divisor is 8 or 4 instead. Sets 0x0C1AB7EC when the result is 0; 0x0C06036A-0x0C06037E reads that flag and 0x0C1AB7E8 to time the BEAT LOOP lamp. Called from loop_divide_position for the beat segment the play position is in.

Beat module setup. While beat_lamp_loop_in is -1 it takes the loop's ring start and end (0x0C7E5038/0x0C7E503C), splits the loop into four beat segments (lengths at 0x0C7E5054.., 247 units each for the 4-beat 128 BPM loop) and zeroes loop_divide_count. Otherwise it returns at once. Its three callers (0x0C008032, 0x0C06EBEE, 0x0C06ECF4) discard the result.

LOOP DIVIDE position map. r4 is the feeder's ring read position. The function finds the beat segment it lies in, folds the offset into the first 1/2^loop_divide_count of that beat (beat_lamp_divided_phase) and returns the ring address of that point, wrapped at the ring size 0x562200. With count 0 the position is unchanged. So the divide replays the start of every beat; it does not move the loop points.

In player states 4/5/7/8 (and 9 with 0x0CD48544 == 3), when r5 is set and 0x0C00B4A4 returns nonzero: if beat_lamp_loop_in is not -1, loop_divide_feed_pos = loop_divide_position(current ring read position). If r5 is clear or 0x0C00B4A4 returns 0, the beat module is reset (0x0C0163D4). Same code at 0x0C06EB24.

Audio feeder: when beat_lamp_loop_in is not -1 and loop_divide_feed_enable (0x0C7E4F24) is set, the frame fetch (0x0C06DF68) reads from loop_divide_feed_pos instead of the normal position, seeding it with that position when it is -1. Same check at 0x0C06E224 behind 0x0C7E4F1C. This is where LOOP DIVIDE becomes audible [emu].
